speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe what happens when you wake up frightened, and do you remember any dreams or feel confused when this happens?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does she have any nightmares that she can recall in detail, and does she exhibit any behaviors during sleep such as sleepwalking or talking? Also, has there been any recent stress or change in her routine?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do these episodes typically occur in the first half of the night or the second half, and does she have any history of anxiety or exposure to scary media? I also want to check for any physical signs, so I will examine her for signs of pain or discomfort.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Met all developmental milestones with no significant medical history. Social history: Attends school regularly, with usual playing habits and interactions with peers. Lives with both parents.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since she recalls the bad dreams and is not confused upon waking, this points toward nightmares rather than sleep terrors, which typically occur in the first half of the night. To confirm this and rule out other causes, I will check her sleep patterns more closely. REQUEST TEST: Polysomnography
